title: Marvell posts Q2 beat, calls Google custom-silicon deal 'game-changing'
subtitle: Marvell reported $2.74B revenue and pointed to a multi-year Google TPU partnership worth up to $120B in cumulative revenue, but the stock fell 8% pre-market as investors read the guide as under-ambitious.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Marvell Technology reported fiscal Q2 earnings of $0.94 per share on $2.74 billion in revenue, beating consensus of $0.93 and $2.71 billion. CEO Matt Murphy told analysts the company's newly announced Google partnership is 'game-changing' and could deliver 'a lot larger' revenue than currently modeled — the deal, disclosed the prior week, could represent up to $120 billion in cumulative revenue over roughly six years subject to milestone gates. Custom silicon, which generated about $1.5 billion in FY26 (roughly 18% of sales), is projected to grow more than 20% in FY27 and more than double in FY28. Despite the beat, MRVL fell as much as 8% pre-market.

The market reaction is the interesting part. Beats without step-changes in guidance no longer clear the bar for AI-adjacent semis; investors now expect a Broadcom-style hyperscaler-custom-chip narrative or they discount the stock. The Google deal supplies the narrative, but the near-term guide did not fully reflect it — Murphy suggested the milestone-gated revenue upside sits mostly beyond FY27, and that timing gap is what pushed the stock lower even as the fundamentals improved.

Custom silicon is where the compute market is quietly reorganizing. Google TPUs, AWS Trainium, Microsoft Maia, Meta MTIA — every hyperscaler now has a first-party accelerator lineage, and Marvell and Broadcom are the two merchant silicon partners actually building those ASICs. That is a very different market structure from 2023, when Nvidia was the single-vendor answer for training and inference alike. Nvidia's Q2 remains larger than every custom-silicon program combined, but the growth curve is bifurcating.

Takeaway for learners: when you read AI-hardware coverage, separate three questions — who designs the chip, who fabricates it, and who runs the workload on it. Google designs its TPU architecture; Marvell (and now Broadcom) co-design and productize; TSMC fabricates; Google's own cloud and internal teams operate. Understanding that chain tells you where margins land and why a $120B headline can still send a stock down.
